paragraphs: Clever Devices builds technology for public transportation providers, meant to help them run more efficiently, spend less and deliver the service riders expect. The company says agencies with anywhere from 50 to 5,000 vehicles have chosen it over more than thirty years.

At the center is CAD/AVL software that gives dispatchers real-time information to monitor and manage the fleet. A vehicle health monitoring product is aimed at cutting repair costs and stretching the mean distance between failures. Onboard, automated passenger announcements are synced with LED signage so riders know where they are. Service planning is handled by the MAIOR scheduling suite, a modular set of planning and optimization tools. For agencies that would rather not run servers, CleverCloud takes on the on-premises hosting burden.

The company tells an unusual origin story, beginning in the early 1980s in the basement of a bar on Long Island. It turned to transit in 1990 when the Americans with Disabilities Act passed. The first product automated the stop announcements bus drivers were required to make. Today the company reports over 600 employees across 12 locations in the United States, Canada, Brazil and Italy. It puts more than 30,000 vehicles on its transportation systems technology. The homepage announces that Hitachi Rail has completed its acquisition of the company.
